summary:
ASTROMIND is a browser-based educational survival game developed to make space exploration and Mars survival concepts more interactive and engaging. In this game, players take on the role of a Mars mission commander and face different survival challenges through three missions containing nine questions. Players must make quick and informed decisions to manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, energy and crew health.

The game combines HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript to provide interactive gameplay, animated visuals, timed challenges, scoring, hints and immediate feedback. Player scores and progress can be saved locally using browser storage.

ASTROMIND addresses the challenge of making STEM learning more engaging by allowing users to learn through decision-making and simulated survival situations. It aims to improve problem-solving skills, resource-management awareness and interest in space exploration.
details:
ASTROMIND – Interactive Mars Survival Simulation

ASTROMIND is an interactive, browser-based educational game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project focuses on making Mars exploration and survival concepts engaging through an interactive simulation.

The game places players in the role of a Mars mission commander, where they must complete survival missions and make important decisions to establish and maintain a colony on Mars. It consists of three progressive missions with nine questions. Each question presents a survival-related situation with four possible answers. Players must make decisions within a limited time while managing five essential resources: oxygen, water, food, energy and crew health.

Every decision affects the player's resources and overall performance. The game includes a countdown timer, hints, scoring, streak bonuses, immediate feedback, mission progression and a leaderboard. These features encourage players to think critically, manage resources wisely and understand the consequences of their decisions.

The project is developed using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript. HTML5 provides the structure, CSS3 handles the interface design and animations, and JavaScript controls the game logic, questions, timer, scoring and resource management. Canvas and SVG are used for graphics and visual elements, while the Web Audio API provides sound effects. LocalStorage saves player scores and progress directly in the browser.

The creativity of ASTROMIND lies in combining educational content with game-based learning. Instead of simply reading about space survival, players experience simulated challenges and learn through their decisions. We considered usability, responsive design, visual appeal, accessibility, gameplay engagement and lightweight performance during development.

ASTROMIND aims to improve problem-solving, decision-making and resource-management skills while encouraging curiosity about space science and exploration.

Future improvements include AI-powered scenarios, multiplayer missions, additional planetary environments and VR/AR experiences.
